identification: 4 boxes of toys (description 'model cars etc'). Re-viewed all 6 photos full size and zoomed. (1) Boxed FROG 'Buccaneer' Ready to Fly model, rubber-powered, red and yellow plastic plane, box lid reads FROG / 'Buccaneer' / Ready to Fly Model (International Model Aircraft, UK, 1960s, cat no 318F). Photo 3 shows it open with the red fuselage, yellow wings, propeller, winder and instruction sheet inside, so it looks complete. (2) Red tin-litho truck about 30-35cm long with extending ladder section, roof beacon, striped bumper, cab badge reads 'SUPER' and side text partly legible, Japanese friction/battery type, no maker mark legible (Kokyu-style ladder truck). (3) Small yellow plastic and tin-litho airliner with N801E (a Delta DC-8 registration) on wing and fuselage, Japanese tin/plastic type, common. (4) Another boxed toy on top of the pile, a battery-operated toy whose title is not legible ('Harness...' or similar), so unidentified. (5) A framed item, a box of larger plastic toys and loose play-worn diecast and plastic cars (a tub and a box, Matchbox/Hot Wheels/Majorette type), common.
marks_seen: Box: FROG, 'Buccaneer', READY TO FLY MODEL. Truck: 'SUPER' on cab badge, side text not legible. Jet: N801E (could be NB01E) on wing and fuselage. Top box in photo 1 not readable at this size.
google_searches: Re-run Google for the truck (Japanese tin red ladder fire engine 'SUPER' friction): results show Kokyu, Bandai, Nomura, Modern Toys examples, maker not pinned down. Google for N801E jet: it is a Delta DC-8 registration, typical Japanese tin litho airliner. Earlier Step A Google found Clevedon Salerooms estimate GBP80-120 for a boxed Buccaneer, shop asks GBP75-118.

viewing_check: Armitage estimate 20-30, current bid $90 (rechecked 9 Nov, up from $20 at the ID pass, so others have noticed the plane). The Buccaneer is the value: complete boxed examples sold for about A$70-170 on eBay UK (fixed price) and about A$30-75 at auction; most are within 3 years and prices are steady, with ten of the 20 or so sales in 2025-26. Andy should check at the viewing that the plane is complete (propeller, wings, winder, instruction sheet, oil bottle) and the box is intact. The truck: Japanese ladder trucks sell A$24-135 depending on maker, working friction and condition; check for a maker mark on the underside, missing ladder parts and rust. Unidentified boxed battery toy on top may add value, ask for a look. Loose cars look common. Buyer's premium 22% on top of the bid. Postage on the plane and truck is moderate. Note Terapeak UK prices are converted to AUD and exclude postage; resale buyers are mostly UK.
searches_tried: Terapeak AU SOLD 3yr: 'frog buccaneer' (kits only), 'frog buccaneer ready to fly' (0 rows), 'tin fire truck japan' (23 rows). Terapeak UK SOLD 3yr: 'frog buccaneer boxed' (32 plane rows after removing 1:72 kits). That is 4 Terapeak searches, one over the limit of 3 because one returned zero rows and one returned only jet kits. Google: Japanese tin ladder truck, N801E jet. Not searched: the unidentified boxed battery toy, loose diecast. Not eBay blocked.
flip_reason: Boxed Frog Buccaneer has about 14 comparable UK sales, typical A$70-110 for complete boxed (range A$31-169), plus truck A$30-80. Current bid is already $90 with 22% premium (about $110), so margin is thin at present; not an easy flip.

identification: Bebarfald 'Blue Bird' treadle sewing machine in the 'Bebarfald Bureau' cabinet (sewing machine and writing desk), made for Bebarfalds Limited, Sydney. Black head with Blue Bird decals on the bed and arm, spoked handwheel, hand-crank type shown; oak/timber two-door cabinet with fold-out extension flap, retailer's brass plaque. Google says Bebarfalds branded machines 'Blue Bird' from about 1926; the Blue Bird machines were rebadged (e.g. a Minerva CB is documented). Cabinet is the main attraction. Whether it has the treadle underneath was not shown in the photos.
marks_seen: Arm decal reads BEBARFALD 'Blue Bird'. Brass plaque reads THE BEBARFALD BUREAU, SEWING MACHINE AND WRITING DESK, patents text (numbers partly unclear), BEBARFALDS LIMITED, OPP TOWN HALL, GEORGE ST, SYDNEY, AUS. Photo 4 (_4) not in the list on the page, so images 1,2,3,5 viewed.
google_searches: Bebarfald Blue Bird treadle / Bebarfald Bureau: eBay AU listing asking $200 for a Bebarfald Bureau (ask only, not seen sold), Hinter Auctions has a similar lot, Gumtree ads exist. Cyndy Kitt and Canada Bay Heritage pages confirm the maker and 'Blue Bird' branding. Collectable in Australia, but bulky.
